Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service New York NY
958 PM EST Wed Nov 18 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Updated to discuss the potential for a coastal storm Sunday 
into Monday.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1) Mostly sunny, dry and above seasonable temps through Saturday.

2) Increasing potential for a coastal low pressure to affect the 
area with wind and rain Sunday into Monday. Minor coastal impacts 
possible due to approaching new moon early next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
.KEY MESSAGE 1...
Good agreement in deep layered ridging through Saturday, albeit
interrupted by a weak shearing PAC shortwave moving thru the NE
US Thu Night/Fri AM. 

At the surface, strong surface high pressure will dominate the 
weather over much of the eastern half of the country through the end 
of the week and into the beginning of the weekend. A moderating 
airmass under ridging will have high temperatures running several 
degrees above normal (upper 50s to middle 60s) thru Saturday.

Given the clear and dry conditions under a weak pressure 
gradient, low temperatures each night through Friday night, and 
potentially Saturday Night, will be largely determined by 
radiational cooling. Overall expect a gradual moderation in 
overnight lows to a few-several degrees above seasonable for 
late week into the weekend, particularly for urban and immediate
coastal areas.

With moderating Tds over the next few days increasing likelihood for 
radiational fog across outlying areas, particularly river valley 
areas. Patchy freezing fog likely in river valleys, and
sheltered interior areas and LI pine barrens tonight and Thu 
Night. This presents a low probability of black ice development 
on elevated surfaces (bridges, overpasses, etc.), particularly 
Thu Night with return flow allowing for a bit of low-level
moisture.


.KEY MESSAGE 2...
Good model agreement on low pressure development along a stalled 
frontal boundary off the SE US coast in vicinity of broad southern 
troughing. NHC is monitoring for potential tropical/sub-tropical 
development of this low through the weekend (currently a 40% 
probability) as this low lifts north along/off the SE US coast and 
the still sufficiently warm gulf stream waters.

Decent NWP/AI model agreement over the last 24 hrs in this 
developing low pressure lifting north along the SE US coast this 
weekend as central US troughing approaches, to near Cape Hatteras 
Sunday AM and then over or very near the area late Sunday into 
Monday morning. 

Ensembles means are generally portraying a low track of weak to 
modest intensity between E LI and 40/70 lat/lon benchmark as it 
makes closest approach to the local region, while deterministic 
AI/NWP and ensemble members models have a considerable track 
spread from over to just SE of the region with considerable 
variance from a weak to strong low pressure system in the
vicinity of our area. With the event still 96 hrs away, still 
quite a bit of forecast sensitivity on strength/timing of 
approaching central US trough and Western Atlantic ridging, and
most importantly the evolution of non-tropical/tropical low 
pressure. Monitor local NWS office and NHC forecasts thru the 
weekend for the latest on this storm.

Overall model trends are pointing to an increasing potential for a 
progressive coastal low pressure affecting the area with a windswept 
soaking rainfall during the Sunday aft into Monday AM period. NBM 
probs for 1" of rainfall in 24 hrs are in the 30-50%, and 2"/24hr in 
the 20-30% range, with a <10% probs of 3-4" in 24hrs. Based on sub-
tropical moisture feed +2-3 STD PWATS, these rainfall amounts look 
quite plausible if a closer approach of the system to the coast 
materializes. Still too early to get into amounts details and peak 
rainfall rates, but a low and localized flash flood threat is 
warranted at this point. 

Similarly low predictability on wind and coastal impact details this 
far out. In general, a track to the SE and E of the region would 
limit wind and coastal flood impacts, with a track over or to the 
west of the region (low prob at this point) increasing the threat 
for a period of strong winds and coastal impacts. Overall, NWP/AI 
probs of 34 kt sustained winds are very low (below 20%) and mainly 
across the ocean waters SE of LI. With that said, potential for a 
period of 20-30mph sustained winds and gusts 35-40mph gusts is 
possible with a low track over/near the coast. As mentioned before, 
a lot of this forecast depends on low pressure evolution off the SE 
US coast over the next 48-72 hrs. Monitor local NWS office and 
NHC forecasts thru the weekend for the latest on this storm. 

Drying and seasonable conditions likely in the wake of this system 
later Monday into early next week.

&&

.AVIATION /03Z THURSDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
High pressure in control through the TAF period. 

VFR. 

A light WNW wind tonight, with speeds falling to around 5 kt or
less. Flow backs SW Thursday afternoon, with speeds remaining 
under 10 kt. With the exception of some high cirrus at times, 
clear skies prevail.

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

Timing of SW wind shift on Thursday could be an hour or two off.

.OUTLOOK FOR 00Z Friday through Monday... 

Thursday night: VFR, light WSW/SW wind.

Friday-Saturday: VFR.

Sunday: Chance of MVFR or lower conditions developing in RA.

Monday: MVFR or lower likely early in RA, improvement possible PM.

Detailed information, including hourly TAF wind component forecasts, 
can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

&&

.MARINE...
Sub SCA conditions expected on all waters through Sunday 
morning as high pressure keeps a weak pressure gradient over 
the area. Winds will mostly be from the NW-W at less than 15kt 
with seas on the ocean no higher than 2 to 3 ft. 

Next chance for SCA or potentially Gale conditions will be 
later Sunday into Monday, dependent on track and intensity of a 
coastal low pressure developing off the SE US coast.
